_meta: Declared, INTENTIONAL rig-vs-shipped-example [net] default mismatches for tools/lint_rig_ini_defaults.py (tooling:TL-SUITE-INIMERGE). A key here is one where ui_test.py's NET_BLOCK deliberately differs from src/mh_dll/mh_net.example.ini's [net] section -- adding an entry needs a real reason, not just a red going away.
host: the rig binds 0.0.0.0 so a remote VM peer (mp_run.py's 2-peer topology, --client <ip>:<script>) can dial in; the shipped example's 127.0.0.1 is a safe loopback-only default for a solo player install. See ui_test.py NET_BLOCK and mp_run.py's host binding.
host_assign: the rig forces host_assign=1 for the harness/verb-driven multi-peer path (the host assigns each joiner its id over the wire, WELCOME) -- U15b (tracker/mp.yaml) made this a hard requirement for that path after a host_assign=0 lane produced duplicate ids. The shipped default (0) is for the MANUAL lobby-seat join flow, which uses declared ids instead. See tools/mp_run.py's host_assign comment and tracker/mp.yaml U15b.
sim_step_ms: the rig pins the deterministic gate's sub-step to 10ms (PINNED_PACING in ui_test.py); the shipped default is 20ms (the adaptive-lookahead pacing a player runs). --ship-pacing drops the pin so a row can measure the shipped rate instead -- see ui_test.py's SHIP_PACING/PINNED_PACING comments and the p13_field_pacing row in tools/test_ui.py.
rx_spin: the rig pins rx_spin=0 with the deterministic gate's pacing (PINNED_PACING in ui_test.py, since P5 2026-07-26); the shipped value is 1 (SHIP_RX_SPIN, net_internal.h -- the example ini said 0 by mistake until dist:RL2 made the code default authoritative, 2026-10-08). --ship-pacing drops the pin to measure the shipped value.
video.window: v0.2.0 moved the ship default to borderless; the rig pins windowed (make_lane.RIG_WINDOW) because every UI baseline was recorded in a windowed frame. Not compared by the lint ([net] only); declared here so the pin has a stated reason.
video.filter: v0.2.0 moved the ship default to area; the rig pins point (make_lane.RIG_FILTER) -- the baselines are point-scaled.
video.vsync: v0.2.0 moved the ship default to 1; the rig pins 0 (make_lane.RIG_VSYNC) -- vsync would pace headless and capped runs to the display.
video.fps_limit: v0.2.0 moved the ship default to 0 (unlimited); the rig pins 60 (make_lane.RIG_FPS_LIMIT, the cap dgVoodoo's FPSLimit used to supply) unless a lane passes --fps-limit.
log.level: v0.2.0 moved the ship default to debug; the rig pins normal (make_lane.RIG_LOG_LEVEL) -- debug turns on the observer logs and the state record the rig's runs were never measured with.
video.backend / input.backend: no exception: the rig always writes both explicitly (make_lane.video_lines / input_lines), so the ship defaults (d3d11 / own) never reach it.
